key_insight: Community-governed collective self-consumption can outperform individually operated PV systems, especially when electricity prices fall and surplus export is poorly remunerated.
engineering_relevance: For PV system designers and operators, the key optimization lever is not only hardware sizing but also coordination rules that improve self-consumption, fairness, and long-term financial viability.
method: Analyzed high-resolution consumption data from a rural PV-sharing community with 24 users.
Compared static, dynamic, and hybrid energy-sharing allocation schemes.
Evaluated scenarios with and without battery storage under current market and regulatory conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that collective self-consumption lowers required PV capacity and investment costs while increasing annual savings versus individual operation, with storage adding limited value in most current-price scenarios.
watch_item: More complex allocation schemes can improve equity and local use, but they introduce governance and implementation complexity that may offset practical benefits.
paper_title: Decision-support strategies for photovoltaic self-consumption under declining electricity prices and limited remuneration of surplus generation
